name: @thetis/gcloud
description: The Google Cloud CLI as tools: run one gcloud command at a time, parsed by gcloud itself and checked against a fixed denylist and your own allow, deny and read-only settings, read any command's help, and see which account, project and policy are in force.

toolGroup.brief: Run Google Cloud CLI (gcloud) commands against GCP projects: compute, GKE, Cloud Run, IAM, storage, logging and the rest.

tools.name: gcloud_run
tools.description: Run one gcloud command and return its exit code, stdout and stderr. Give the words after `gcloud` as `args` (preferred) or one `command` line; they are passed as arguments, never to a shell, so pipes, redirection, `&&` and `$(...)` do not work: run one command per call and filter with gcloud's own --filter, --format and --limit. gcloud parses the line first (meta lint-gcloud-commands); a malformed one is refused without running. Refused always: ssh, tunnels, `interactive`, `init`, `auth login`, the print-token commands, `components`. The person's allow/deny/read-only settings apply on top. This can create, change and delete real cloud resources: say what a mutating command will do before running it. Tips: pass --project=ID explicitly when unsure; use --format=json(field,…) projections and --limit to keep output small; --quiet is implied (prompts are disabled); add --async to long creates; `gcloud logging read` needs --limit.

args.description: The command as a list of words after `gcloud`, e.g. ["compute", "instances", "list", "--project=my-proj", "--format=json(name,zone.basename(),status)"]. A filter or other value with spaces is one element.

command.description: The same as one line, split like a shell would split words (quotes honoured, nothing expanded). Use when args is awkward.

dry_run.description: Only parse and check the command against the policy; run nothing.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait, 5-600. Defaults to the package's timeoutMs (120s).

cwd.description: Directory to run in, relative to home: for commands that read local files (builds submit, run deploy --source, storage cp).

tools.name: gcloud_help
tools.description: Read gcloud's help for a command or group (its synopsis, flags and examples), or search all help text. Use it before gcloud_run when unsure of a flag, instead of guessing.

args.description: The command path without flags, e.g. ["run", "deploy"] or ["beta", "container", "clusters"].

command.description: The command path as one line, e.g. "compute instances create".

search.description: Search every command's help for these terms instead (gcloud help -- TERMS).

full.description: Return up to 18000 characters instead of 9000.

tools.name: gcloud_status
tools.description: Show what gcloud_run will run as: the SDK version, the credentialed accounts and which is active, the default project, region and zone, and the allow/deny/read-only policy in force. Call it first, and whenever a command fails on auth or project.

project.help: Default project id (CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT). A --project flag in a command still wins.

account.help: Which credentialed account to use when gcloud holds several (CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT).

credentialsJson.help: A service account key (the whole JSON). Written to a private file under home for each call and removed after it. The simplest way to give this space credentials; prefer a least-privilege service account.

credentialFile.help: Path to a credentials file gcloud should use instead (CLOUDSDK_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_FILE_OVERRIDE): a service account key or an external-account (workload identity federation) config.

impersonateServiceAccount.help: Act as this service account (CLOUDSDK_AUTH_IMPERSONATE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT). The credential needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on it.

billingProject.help: Quota/billing project for APIs that need one (CLOUDSDK_CORE_BILLING_QUOTA_PROJECT).

configDir.help: gcloud's config directory (CLOUDSDK_CONFIG). Defaults to ~/.config/gcloud in this space.

mode.help: `full` (default) or `read-only`. read-only admits only commands whose verb reads (list, describe, get-iam-policy, read, …); full admits anything the lists allow.

allow.help: If set, only these commands or groups run: a comma-separated list or a JSON array, e.g. `compute instances, run services, beta run`. An entry admits exactly the release track it names (gcloud-mcp's rule).

deny.help: Commands or groups refused on top of the fixed denylist: a comma-separated list or a JSON array, e.g. `projects delete, iam, alpha`. A GA entry denies its alpha and beta variants too.

gcloudPath.help: Full path to the gcloud executable when it is not on the PATH.

timeoutMs.help: Default per-command timeout in milliseconds, clamped to 5000-600000.
